apps.name: Intervals: What, Why and How
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: what intervals are, and how they shape melody, transposition, inversion, singing, tension, chords, keys and atonal music.

apps.name: Modes: The Simple Truth
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: the same notes from any degree of any major scale, parallel modes, major and minor families, PADMIL in any key, modal key signatures, naming modes by ear from scales and chord progressions, and modes beyond the diatonic.

apps.name: Understanding Keys, Scale Degrees and Tendency Tones
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: scale-degree names, the subtonic and leading tone, stable and tendency tones and how they resolve, and telling a key from its relative major or minor.

apps.name: Understanding Rhythm Notation
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: showing the beat, common errors, beaming, ties and slurs, rhythm terms from syncopation to metric modulation, and notating lyrics.

apps.name: Understanding Harmonic Succession
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: chord functions, the progression chart, the phrase model, circle progressions, retrogressions, chord streams, and structural vs. embellishing chords.

apps.name: Understanding Cadences
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: authentic (perfect and imperfect), half, plagal, deceptive and other cadences, degrees of closure, elision and turnarounds, in four voices in any key.

apps.name: Understanding Non-Chord Tones
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: passing and neighbor tones, appoggiaturas, escape tones, suspensions and their figures, retardations, anticipations, double neighbors and pedal tones.

apps.name: Understanding Secondary Function Chords
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: name the chord, read its quality, find its target and write the Roman numeral for secondary dominants, leading-tone chords and pre-dominants, with examples to play in any key.

apps.name: Understanding Chromatic Chords
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson in four parts: mode mixture and the Picardy third, the Neapolitan (♭II), Italian, French and German augmented sixth chords, and chromatic mediants, with examples to play in any key.

apps.name: Understanding Extended and Altered Chords
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: seventh chords, 6, add and sus chords, 9ths, 11ths and 13ths, altered tones, writing chord symbols, omissions and N.C.

apps.name: Understanding Modulation
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: modulation vs. tonicization, closely related keys, pivot chords of every kind, direct modulation and turnarounds.

apps.name: Understanding Voice Motion and Polyphony
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: voice ranges, the four kinds of motion, forbidden parallels, spacing and crossing, and the textures of polyphony from drone and organum to canon and heterophony, with sound examples.

apps.name: Understanding Part-Writing
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: melodic principles, spacing and doubling, tendency tones, parallels, connecting triads, and resolving V⁷ and vii°⁷ in four voices.

apps.name: Understanding Motive and Sequence
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: motives and how they change (transposition, inversion, retrograde, augmentation, fragmentation), and tonal, real and modified sequences.

apps.name: Understanding Phrases and Phrase Combinations
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: phrases and sub-phrases, the sentence, periods, phrase groups, three-phrase and double periods.

apps.name: Understanding Musical Forms
apps.blurb: An interactive lesson: binary, ternary, strophic and song forms, rondo, variations, sonata form and the sections of popular songs, with listening examples.

apps.name: Chord Figures and Symbols
apps.blurb: Spell triads and seventh chords, read them on the grand staff, turn figured bass into chord symbols, and label inversions.

apps.name: Chord Extensions
apps.blurb: Spell 9th, 11th, 13th and altered chords from their symbols, and name them from the staff.

apps.name: Modes
apps.blurb: Spell modes, name them from the staff, find modal key signatures with PADMIL, and review modal pitches.

apps.name: Keys, Scale Degrees and Tendency Tones
apps.blurb: Name scale degrees and their pitches, resolve tendency tones, and tell a key from its relative major or minor.

apps.name: Harmonic Succession
apps.blurb: Chord functions, progression vs. retrogression, the phrase model, embellishing chords, and circle progressions and chord streams.

apps.name: Cadences
apps.blurb: Name cadences in four voices and by ear, read them from chord symbols, and judge their closure.

apps.name: Non-Chord Tones
apps.blurb: Name and find non-chord tones in melodies, label suspension figures, and review how each type is approached and left.

apps.name: Secondary Function Chords
apps.blurb: Identify secondary dominants, leading-tone chords and pre-dominants, label them in any key, find them in progressions, and spell them from Roman numerals.

apps.name: Chromatic Chords
apps.blurb: Label and spell borrowed, Neapolitan and augmented sixth chords in any key, find them in progressions, tell borrowed chords from secondary ones, and work with chromatic mediants.

apps.name: Key Modulation
apps.blurb: Name the modulation method, find and label pivot chords, and judge key relationships.

apps.name: Voice Motion and Polyphony
apps.blurb: Name motion types, spot parallel 5ths and octaves, check SATB ranges and spacing, and identify textures by ear.

apps.name: Part-Writing
apps.blurb: Find the error in four-voice writing, choose doublings, resolve tendency tones, and recognize the ways to resolve V⁷.

apps.name: Motive and Sequence
apps.blurb: Name how a motive is changed and tell tonal, real and modified sequences apart.

apps.name: Phrases and Phrase Combinations
apps.blurb: Name how two phrases combine on the staff, read phrase diagrams, and review phrase terms.

apps.name: Musical Forms
apps.blurb: Name forms from their plans and by ear, review sonata form, and identify the sections of popular songs.

apps.name: Rhythm Notation
apps.blurb: Complete bars, name meters, fix beaming, and spot syncopation, hemiola and anacrusis.

apps.name: Rhythm Performance
apps.blurb: Read a rhythm, hear the count-in, then tap or clap it. Every note is checked for timing, with levels from quarter notes to syncopation and triplets.

apps.name: Strings
apps.blurb: Violin to bass: open strings and string numbers, natural and artificial harmonics, bowings and color effects.

apps.name: Winds & Brass
apps.blurb: Woodwind and brass instruments, score order and scoring shorthand, valves and partials, mutes and techniques.

apps.name: Percussion
apps.blurb: Drums, mallets and metals: materials, beaters, playing logistics and percussion notation.

apps.name: Score and Parts Preparation
apps.blurb: What professional scores and parts must include, and the typesetting conventions players expect.

apps.name: Orchestration Foreign Terms
apps.blurb: Instrument names and score terms in English, French, German and Italian.

apps.name: Instrument Transpositions
apps.blurb: Which instruments transpose and by how much: read parts at concert pitch, write for any instrument, and transpose key signatures.

apps.name: Ear Training
apps.blurb: Sing intervals above a given note and short melodic patterns (the app listens), name chord qualities, and take melodic dictation.

apps.name: Metronome
apps.blurb: Tap a tempo or pick a traditional metronome marking; set meters, groupings, accents and subdivisions; click or drum beats (plain or swing); silent-bar and speed trainers.

apps.name: Drone
apps.blurb: A steady drone on one note or a chord, in equal temperament, Pythagorean tuning, or just intonation (5-, 7-, 11- or 13-limit).

apps.name: Shadow Tuner
apps.blurb: A tuner that sings a reference pitch back to you while you play or sing.
